strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine data scarcity bottleneck for RDB foundation models
Principled relational prior design with formal universality theorem (D.23) and grounded assumptions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation on 19 diverse tasks with 10 random seeds and multiple evaluation protocols
Substantial efficiency gains: 3-8× faster inference, 2.6M parameters vs. 100M+ for competitors, only 2M synthetic datasets for pre-training
Fair comparison setup: providing identical DFS-linearized features to all baselines for architectural comparison
Solid theoretical treatment with rigorous proofs mapping high-level principles to constructive instantiations
Thoughtful data generation pipeline with hybrid sampling, temporal vocabulary, and practical implementation details
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: binary classification only, with multi-class and regression deferred to future work, constraining practical applicability

Contradiction between 'relational' framing and heavy reliance on DFS linearization—method converts RDB reasoning to tabular reasoning via deterministic feature engineering, undermining claims of native relational reasoning
Modest empirical improvements: averaging ~65% for RDB-PFN vs. ~64% for TabPFNv2.5 across tasks; individual task gains typically 1-3%

Synthetic data validity not established: no systematic evaluation of distribution match with real RDBs beyond visual correlation matrices; temporal vocabulary primitives (3 types) are coarse abstractions
Unfair baseline comparisons: Griffin evaluated with idealized oracle ensemble; RT's different methodology not empirically compared; graph-based RDB models relegated to appendix

Critical ablations missing: curriculum learning contribution, relational prior components (temporal vocabulary, preferential attachment, latent states), training dataset size sensitivity, and candidate set size robustness
No distribution shift analysis: how does performance degrade when real databases significantly deviate from synthetic prior distribution?
Insufficient analysis of learned patterns: no attention visualization, failure-mode characterization, or interpretation of which relational patterns the model exploits
Experimental setup biases: inconsistent baseline hyperparameter tuning, post-hoc adaptation of LimiX preprocessing, DFS engineering advantage for proposed method
Acyclic schema assumption excludes cyclic relationships present in production databases despite claim of 95% acyclicity coverage
